question: \(d\) is a direction vector of line \(l\). Which of the following must also be a direction vector of \(l\)?
solution: Multiplying a direction vector by a nonzero real number produces a vector that remains parallel to the line, so it is still a direction vector. The zero vector cannot serve as a direction vector.
